reason: E1 supports grain refinement and a ~21% strength increase for a different HEA (CrFeCuMnNi) with Al2O3, but provides no evidence for chemical inertness in caloric MM'X systems, no data on 3 vol% percolation limits, and no demonstration of uniform dispersion in the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy. E2 only describes general mechanical testing methods. Thus, the key premises about caloric compatibility, optimal volume fraction, and applicability to this alloy are unsupported.
premises: Al2O3 particles refine grain size via Zener pinning in HEA composites
Al2O3 particles increase compressive strength in HEA composites
Al2O3 particles are chemically inert with respect to caloric phase transformations
A 3 vol% Al2O3 addition avoids percolation or excessive embrittlement
Mechanical alloying and forging can uniformly disperse Al2O3 in an HEA matrix
